content:
A laboratory mechanism does not automatically explain an online population
Online settings differ in visibility, responsibility, coordination costs, duplicate effort and how anyone knows that help occurred. A bystander mechanism is a testable candidate among these possibilities. The essay offers no direct estimate identifying it as the dominant cause of internet inaction.

The reward mechanism could optimize its own display
Thanks, visible acknowledgment and referral credit might motivate useful work. They can also reward actions that are easy to display, encourage gaming or privilege well-connected participants. Test verified downstream benefit, duplication and cost before treating more visible activity as more effective help.

A successful counterexample changes the question
Acknowledging an online cooperative success prevents the argument from establishing a general inability to act together. The useful question becomes which infrastructure, incentives and task properties support action. Compare successes with failures instead of using only the latter to diagnose a universal psychological defect.
